root_cause.text: The nft_set_pipapo garbage collector freed expired elements during commit while they were still reachable from the live pipapo match structure, so readers could still access elements after they had been queued for RCU reclamation, causing a use-after-free and long non-preemptible GC stalls.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explains that “Expired elements are still exposed to both the packet path and userspace dumpers via the live copy of the data structure” and that “call_rcu() does not protect us,” then changes `pipapo_gc()` into `pipapo_gc_scan()` plus `pipapo_gc_queue()` so elements are only queued for freeing after `rcu_replace_pointer(priv->match, priv->clone, ...)` swaps clone and live pointers in `nft_pipapo_commit()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to report remaining nft transaction GC batch space.
intent_record.what: A new static inline helper function named `nft_trans_gc_space()` was added to the `nft_trans_gc` code. It takes a `const struct nft_trans_gc *trans` and returns `NFT_TRANS_GC_BATCHCOUNT - trans->count`.
intent_record.how: This exposes the remaining available capacity in an NFT garbage-collection transaction batch, allowing callers to determine how many more items can be added before reaching the batch limit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused GC space helper function.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the static function `nft_trans_gc_space(struct nft_trans_gc *trans)`, which previously returned `NFT_TRANS_GC_BATCHCOUNT - trans->count`.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the standalone helper used to compute remaining GC batch capacity, so any callers must now use an alternative direct calculation or no longer rely on this function; it does not itself add new runtime behavior in the shown hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename the pipapo GC helper to reflect that it scans expired entries and links them to the GC list.
intent_record.what: The function comment was updated to describe scanning expired entries and linking them to the GC list instead of destroying start and end elements, and the function name was renamed from `pipapo_gc` to `pipapo_gc_scan` while keeping the same parameters and body start.
intent_record.how: This changes the function's identified role in the code from a garbage-collection/destruction step to a scanning/linking step, which clarifies that it prepares expired entries for later GC handling rather than directly destroying them at this point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Link the GC object into the private GC list before processing to ensure it is properly tracked during pipapo garbage collection.
intent_record.what: A new `list_add(&gc->list, &priv->gc_head);` call was inserted near the start of `pipapo_gc()` immediately after the `gc` null check and before the `while` loop.
intent_record.how: This makes the newly allocated or selected `gc` object become part of `priv->gc_head` before garbage collection processing continues, so it will be tracked in the list during later GC handling instead of remaining unlinked.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix pipapo GC processing to allocate a new GC transaction when the current one runs out of space.
intent_record.what: In `pipapo_gc()`, the code handling an expired element no longer unconditionally calls `nft_trans_gc_queue_sync(gc, GFP_KERNEL)` before deactivation. Instead, it first checks `nft_trans_gc_space(gc)`, and only if there is no space does it allocate a new GC transaction with `nft_trans_gc_alloc(set, 0, GFP_KERNEL)`, return early on allocation failure, and add the new GC object to `priv->gc_head` with `list_add(&gc->list, &priv->gc_head)`.
intent_record.how: This changes garbage-collection handling so the function can continue processing expired elements even when the current GC transaction is full by creating a new GC transaction batch. It prevents premature termination caused by lack of GC space and ensures expired pipapo elements are still deactivated and dropped when additional GC capacity is needed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor pipapo garbage collection to always run a catchall GC cycle and flush queued GC transactions so expired elements are reliably freed.
intent_record.what: The original `pipapo_gc()` ending `gc = nft_trans_gc_catchall_sync(gc);` and its `if (gc) { ... priv->last_gc = jiffies; }` block were replaced by setting `priv->last_gc = jiffies;` directly, then a new helper `pipapo_gc_queue(struct nft_set *set)` was added. The new helper allocates a GC transaction with `nft_trans_gc_alloc(set, 0, GFP_KERNEL)`, runs `nft_trans_gc_catchall_sync(gc)`, queues the result with `nft_trans_gc_queue_sync_done(gc)` if present, and then iterates over `priv->gc_head` with `list_for_each_entry_safe()` to `list_del()` and `nft_trans_gc_queue_sync_done()` each queued GC element.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior changes from only syncing a catchall GC transaction at the end of `pipapo_gc()` to also always performing a catchall GC cycle and explicitly draining any previously queued GC work from `priv->gc_head`. This ensures expired elements and deferred GC transactions are actually finalized and freed, rather than potentially remaining queued indefinitely, and it updates `last_gc` when GC runs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify the commit path comment to note when expired pipapo elements can safely be queued for reclaim.
intent_record.what: The comment above `nft_pipapo_commit()` was extended with four new lines explaining that once the live copy is replaced by the clone, expired elements collected by `pipapo_gc_scan()` may be safely queued for memory reclamation.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime code behavior; it documents the ordering constraint that reclamation of expired elements must happen only after the live set has been swapped out, clarifying the safe point for freeing collected entries.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch nft_pipapo_commit() to the correct garbage-collection scan routine during timed GC processing.
intent_record.what: In nft_pipapo_commit(), the call inside the garbage-collection time check was changed from pipapo_gc(set, priv->clone) to pipapo_gc_scan(set, priv->clone).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the commit path now invokes the scan-oriented garbage collection routine instead of the previous GC routine when the GC interval has elapsed, altering which cleanup logic runs during set commit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Queue pipapo garbage collection after commit so deferred cleanup runs correctly.
intent_record.what: A new call to `pipapo_gc_queue(set);` was added at the end of `nft_pipapo_commit(struct nft_set *set)`, after the optional `call_rcu(&old->rcu, pipapo_reclaim_match);` block.
intent_record.how: After a successful commit, the code now schedules the pipapo set for garbage collection processing. This ensures deferred cleanup work is queued following updates, rather than leaving it unscheduled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the pipapo garbage-collection list head during setup to prevent use of an uninitialized list.
intent_record.what: A call to INIT_LIST_HEAD(&priv->gc_head) was added in nft_pipapo_init() immediately before rcu_assign_pointer(priv->match, m); no existing lines were removed or altered.
intent_record.how: This initializes the gc_head list head for the pipapo private data during set setup, ensuring the garbage-collection list starts in a valid empty state before the structure is used at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a teardown-time warning to detect and flag non-empty pipapo GC state during set destruction.
intent_record.what: A single `WARN_ON_ONCE(!list_empty(&priv->gc_head));` check was inserted at the start of `nft_pipapo_destroy()`, before dereferencing `priv->match` and before the existing clone teardown logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the destroy path now emits a one-time warning if the `gc_head` list is not empty when the pipapo set is being destroyed, which helps detect unexpected leftover garbage-collection entries during teardown without changing normal control flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a garbage-collection list head to nft_pipapo for tracking pending memory reclamation entries.
intent_record.what: The struct nft_pipapo definition gains a new field named gc_head of type struct list_head, and the accompanying comment is updated to document it as a list of nft_trans_gc objects queued for memory reclaim.
intent_record.how: This adds per-nft_pipapo list storage for garbage-collection transactions, allowing the code to accumulate reclaimable items for later cleanup instead of handling them elsewhere.

consistency_review.reason: Hunk 7 is about selecting the correct GC scan routine during timed GC processing, while Hunk 4 is about allocating a new GC transaction when the current one is full; these address different failure modes and are not the same coherent fix.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix pipapo garbage collection handling so deferred cleanup is correctly tracked, queued after commit, and fully processed.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a helper to report remaining NFT transaction GC batch space, which is unrelated to the pipapo GC use-after-free caused by freeing elements still reachable from the live match structure.
The change only removes an unused GC space helper function and does not alter pipapo garbage collection, RCU lifetime handling, or the commit-time freeing behavior that caused the use-after-free.

This change is only a helper rename/commentary about GC scanning and list linking. It does not alter the lifetime handling, RCU reclamation, or the commit-time freeing behavior that caused the use-after-free.

The changes directly target pipapo GC timing and tracking, moving cleanup to after commit and ensuring queued GC work is properly processed. This matches the root cause where elements were freed too early while still reachable, leading to UAF and GC stalls.

The change directly targets pipapo commit-time garbage collection and switches to the correct scan routine during timed GC processing, which matches the root cause involving premature freeing of still-reachable elements and GC behavior.

The change targets the pipapo commit/GC path described in the root cause, specifically clarifying when expired elements may be safely queued for reclamation. This is directly related to the premature freeing/RCU lifetime issue that caused the use-after-free.

This change only initializes the pipapo GC list head to avoid using an uninitialized list. It does not address the root cause where expired elements were freed during commit while still reachable from the live match structure, leading to UAF and GC stalls.

This change only adds a teardown-time warning to detect non-empty pipapo GC state during set destruction. It does not fix the root cause of freeing still-reachable elements during commit or address the resulting UAF/GC stall behavior.

The change adds GC tracking for nft_pipapo pending reclamation entries, which directly relates to the root cause where expired elements were freed/queued while still reachable. This is part of fixing the lifetime/RCU reclamation handling that caused the use-after-free.

The change is about handling pipapo GC transaction space exhaustion by allocating a new transaction. It does not address the root cause of freeing still-reachable elements during commit or the resulting use-after-free/RCU reclamation issue.

This is the actual call that performs pipapo garbage collection in the commit path. The vulnerability stems from freeing expired elements during commit, and this statement embodies that premature reclamation.

This statement shows the GC transaction being processed in a synchronous commit-time path. If expired elements are reclaimed here before the new match is safely installed and old readers are gone, it contributes to the use-after-free.

This conditional selects the timed GC path during commit, which is the path that prematurely triggered reclamation of still-reachable elements.
This synchronous GC processing step is part of the commit-time reclamation flow that could free expired elements before readers had dropped references.
This completes the synchronous GC transaction handling in the vulnerable commit path, contributing to premature reclamation before safe deferred cleanup.

Author: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

    netfilter: nf_tables: adapt set backend to use GC transaction API

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is no longer present in this function. The old buggy behavior was to destroy expired elements directly while iterating the live match structure: `if (nft_set_elem_expired(&e->ext) && !nft_set_elem_mark_busy(&e->ext)) { ... rcu_barrier(); nft_set_elem_destroy(set, e, true); }`. In the shown code, that path has been replaced with GC transaction handling: `gc = nft_trans_gc_alloc(set, 0, GFP_KERNEL);`, `gc = nft_trans_gc_queue_sync(gc, GFP_ATOMIC);`, `nft_pipapo_gc_deactivate(net, set, e);`, `pipapo_drop(m, rulemap);`, and `nft_trans_gc_elem_add(gc, e);`. This means elements are deactivated before being queued for later reclamation, instead of being freed in-place while still reachable. The catchall handling also moved from immediate destruction (`nft_set_elem_destroy`) to `nft_trans_gc_catchall(gc, 0)` and `nft_trans_gc_queue_sync_done(gc)`, which matches the fix described for the use-after-free issue.
